name: Horcrux
banner: Daily builds for testing. Not for production.
tagline: Horcrux is a free, Gentoo-based hypervisor with a web UI: VMs, containers and clusters. Pre-1.0.
lead: A Gentoo-based hypervisor with a web UI, in the style of Proxmox VE: virtual machines, containers, storage and clusters, written in Rust.
what_html:
Horcrux manages QEMU/KVM, LXD and Incus virtual machines and LXC, LXD, Incus, Docker and Podman containers from one web UI, CLI and API. It adds clustering with live migration and HA, a distributed firewall, backups and RBAC. It is built for Gentoo: the ebuild and USE flags choose which backends get compiled in.

It is a one-person project in early development. It aims at Proxmox VE-style functionality; it does not claim parity yet.
status: Horcrux is version 0.1.x. APIs, configuration and on-disk formats can still change between builds. Use test hardware or a VM.
works: Daily ISO: a QEMU test boots it, installs it (unattended, serial wizard and VGA wizard, ext4, XFS and ZFS mirror, UEFI and BIOS), reboots from disk and logs in to the web UI.
Nightly tests on real QEMU/KVM guests: snapshots, backup and restore, API restarts and crashes, live migration, HA failover on 3 nodes, save state on host shutdown.
Unit and integration tests against real services (LDAP, OIDC, nftables, CNI, Docker, k3s) on every change.
gaps: No stable release. No upgrade or rollback test of an installed system yet.
The graphical installer is in progress; today the installer is a text wizard.
Real-hardware testing has only just started and has already found bugs (a CPU-specific crash, fixed on main).
aarch64 is built and tested only under QEMU emulation (no real arm64 hardware yet); riscv64 is not built.
isos: x86_64 Desktop (UEFI + BIOS, GNOME, encrypted ZFS + hibernate)
dl_note: The aarch64 build is tested under QEMU emulation, not on real arm64 hardware.
shots: File system: ext4, XFS or a ZFS mirror
